title: erase
summary: Remove substring occurrences from text inputs in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: Runs on the CPU. RunMat has no resident text storage, so GPU-resident numeric arguments are rejected before gather.

description: `erase(text, pattern)` removes every occurrence of `pattern` from `text`. Supported text/pattern forms and expansion behavior match MATLAB semantics.
behaviors: String inputs stay as strings. Missing string scalars (`<missing>`) propagate unchanged.
String arrays preserve their size and orientation. Each element has every supplied pattern removed.
Character arrays are processed row by row. Rows shrink as characters are removed and are padded with spaces so the result remains a rectangular char array.
Cell arrays must contain string scalars or character vectors. The result is a cell array with the same shape whose elements reflect the removed substrings.

The `pattern` input can be a string scalar, string array, character array, or cell array of character vectors/string scalars. Provide either a scalar pattern or a list; an empty list leaves `text` unchanged.
String, character, and cell matches are treated literally. RunMat pattern objects use their compiled pattern expression, matching the documented pattern-object form.
Both arguments are text or pattern values. Numeric values, including every typed-integer class and nested resident numeric values, are rejected before any provider access.

examples.description: Remove a single word from a string scalar
examples.input:
txt = "RunMat accelerates MATLAB code";
clean = erase(txt, "accelerates ")

examples.description: Remove multiple substrings from each element of a string array
Erase characters from a character array while preserving padding
Remove substrings from a cell array of text
Provide an empty pattern list to leave the text unchanged

faqs.question: Can I remove multiple patterns at once?
faqs.answer: Yes. Supply `pattern` as a string array or cell array. Each pattern is removed in order from every element of the input text.

faqs.question: What happens if `pattern` is empty?
faqs.answer: An empty pattern list leaves the input unchanged. Empty string patterns are ignored because removing empty text would have no effect.

faqs.question: Does `erase` modify the original data?
faqs.answer: No. It returns a new value with substrings removed. The input variables remain unchanged.

faqs.question: How are missing string scalars handled?
faqs.answer: They propagate unchanged. Calling `erase` on `<missing>` returns `<missing>`, matching MATLAB.

faqs.question: Can `erase` operate on GPU-resident data?
faqs.answer: Indirectly. RunMat automatically gathers GPU values to the host, performs the removal, and returns a host result. No explicit `gpuArray` calls are required.

faqs.question: How do I remove substrings using patterns or regular expressions?
faqs.answer: Use `replace` for literal substitution or `regexprep` for regular expressions when you need pattern-based removal rather than literal substring erasure.

gpu_residency: No. `erase` accepts host text and pattern values only. GPU-resident numeric values are not text and are rejected before provider access.
gpu_behavior: `erase` executes on host text containers. Resident numeric arguments, including values nested in cells, are rejected without downloading; providers do not implement a text kernel for this builtin.
